name: Neo-nationalism
summary: Neo-nationalism is a nationalist and right-populist current of the 2010s that defends national identity, sovereignty and borders against globalisation, supranational bodies such as the EU, and mass immigration. It usually defines the nation by shared history and culture rather than race, backs protectionism and nation-first policy, and casts political and cultural elites as detached from ordinary citizens.
scope: The mainstream Western and Central European strand since about 2015, as seen in Trump's America First address and Orban's illiberal-state speech, with the Wikipedia overview and Bergmann's nativist-populism analysis as reference. Excludes classical ethnic nationalism and the explicitly racial far right, and national variants in Asia and the Middle East that the overview also lists.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Adherents are split: welfare-chauvinist parties often back public health for citizens while market-leaning ones do not; the movement has no common line, so this is inferred as neutral.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic stagnation among working and middle classes drives support, but leaders differ on wage floors; no shared position is documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement criticizes the post-Cold War free-market consensus and neoliberal deals, so adherents lean against a blanket claim of market superiority; inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Some neo-nationalist governments protect strategic firms while others privatize; no common doctrine, inferred as split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Populist rhetoric attacks elites, yet right-leaning leaders often cut top taxes; adherents are genuinely split.

unions-good.rationale: Appeal to blue-collar voters coexists with distrust of organized labor in several movements; inferred as split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Most right-wing neo-nationalists defend private property, though without making it a distinctive tenet; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Hostility to globalist corporations is mixed with business-friendly deregulation in practice; inferred as split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Orban's work-based society trims benefits for the idle, but neo-nationalists broadly defend welfare for citizens, so a blanket cut is leaned against; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a theme of neo-nationalism, which is nation-centred rather than class-structural; inferred disagreement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The movement stresses security against terrorism and praises police and military, so surveillance for that purpose is likely accepted; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cultural-traditionalist wing and law-and-order stance suggest opposition, though not a core theme; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Neo-nationalists present themselves as targets of censorship by liberal elites and oppose speech restrictions; inferred from anti-elite framing.

strong-leader.rationale: Trump's address presents the leader as acting for the people against a gridlocked capital, and the movement has produced personalist leaders such as Orban and Erdogan.

state-harmful.rationale: Neo-nationalism holds up the nation-state as the vehicle of self-determination and is the opposite of anti-statism.

limit-guns.rationale: Right-leaning adherents generally oppose strict gun limits (notably in the US) though not as a core tenet; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Trump's address praises troops and law enforcement and laments depleted military; law-and-order is a standard theme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Cultural traditionalism points toward opposition; not central, so inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement centres on national sovereignty against supranational bodies rather than devolution; inferred mild disagreement.

rehabilitation.rationale: Tough-on-crime orientation implies preference for punishment; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Orban's speech ties his state to protecting families, and the movement defends traditional heritage; documented but not universal.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Strands vary (some Western neo-nationalists accept it), but the typical adherent opposes; contested so low.

abortion-legal.rationale: Religious-traditionalist strands oppose, though secular strands differ; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wikipedia notes religion is used as national tradition in some cases (Poland, Hungary) but not in others; mixed so low.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Neo-nationalism is tied to anti-multiculturalism and white identity politics in the US, rejecting remedial programs; inferred from that.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditionalist wing rejects this claim; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending national identity, symbolic heritage, art and folk traditions is a defining trait of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents want to roll back change but through radical populist politics; split between conservative and disruptive stances.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to immigration is a core defining feature of neo-nationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement pits the nation-state against supranational regimes like the EU and rejects a global governance.

free-trade.rationale: It is protectionist and criticizes free-trade deals and the post-Cold War trade consensus.

nation-first.rationale: Trump's address states every nation's right to put its own interests first and pledges America First.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The address says the US will not impose its way of life and criticizes costly overseas engagement; moderate rejection.

open-borders.rationale: Border defence is central: the address criticizes defending other nations' borders while not defending its own.

limit-growth.rationale: Protectionist job-focused agenda favours growth; not directly addressed, inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anti-globalist movements generally resist international climate regimes; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources describe no neo-nationalist view on technology as a cure-all, so the answer is a neutral inference.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by sources; adherents differ by country.

revolution-justified.rationale: Movement works largely through elections and existing institutions; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: The address pits ordinary people against an establishment that protects itself, a typical populist anti-technocratic stance.

central-planning.rationale: Not a planned-economy ideology; inferred disagreement.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism is not discussed in sources on neo-nationalism, which is about nation and identity; mild disagreement inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Neither the sources nor the movement's platforms address land taxation, so neutral is the only honest answer.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Right-leaning adherents generally oppose estate taxes; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Orban's work-based society ties benefits to work; inferred against unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The address calls for protection from other countries' making goods and taking jobs, and Wikipedia describes the movement as protectionist.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Neo-nationalist governments use state-led industrial and economic nationalism against neoliberal trade deals; moderate.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist property schemes are not part of documented neo-nationalism; adherents are indifferent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing wages is a communist aim with no place in a nation-centred ideology, so strong disagreement is inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Some populists attack central banks, but abolition is not a mainstream plank; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised wage bodies are not a documented neo-nationalist plank, and leaders in different countries differ.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wikipedia notes authoritarian forms in China and Saudi Arabia but typical Western variants compete in elections; contested.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Monarchy matters in Japan or Saudi Arabia but not in Western variants, so adherents are split by country.

democracy-best.rationale: Orban's illiberal state declares liberal democracy not the model; most adherents claim democratic legitimacy while criticizing liberal constraints, so split.

direct-votes.rationale: Populists often favour referendums such as Brexit; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Council democracy is a left-wing idea contrary to nation-centred electoral politics; inferred disagreement.

right-to-secede.rationale: The movement stresses national unity, though it can back self-determination for its own nation; inferred mild disagreement.

natural-rulers.rationale: The populist framing sets the people against self-serving elites, against inherent rulers; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream adherents disavow violence but the movement's extremes differ; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: The address urges unity and leading by example rather than glorifying war; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion treated as national heritage in several cases; inferred mild disagreement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religious heritage is valued culturally but scriptural law is not a plank; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Strong state security role is central; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: The address laments a depleted military and praises troops; strength is emphasised.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia says neo-nationalism defines membership by historical association rather than ethnic or racial criteria, unlike classical nationalism, though critics dispute this.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The address frames the divide as people versus political elite and calls for unity rather than class conflict.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Particular national self-interest over group rights; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hostile to supranational unions generally, though some envisage civilizational blocs; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective national self-interest is endorsed, individual not addressed; neutral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Nation-centred outlook ranks national community over individual claims; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is not addressed by neo-nationalism; no common view among adherents.

limit-population.rationale: Pro-natalist leanings in Hungary and others; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Neo-nationalists want to bring back factory jobs, so they reject the claim that industry has been a disaster; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not a movement theme; inferred mild disagreement.

human-enhancement.rationale: Traditionalist and heritage-defending leanings suggest reluctance about transhumanist aims; inferred, not documented.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Distrust of expert rule and favours accountable leaders; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The security emphasis and trust in police suggest favouring government access; inferred from that, not stated.

restore-past-order.rationale: Trump's address promises to end carnage and restore the nation, and the movement answers globalisation by defending the past order of national identity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Populists often claim pragmatism while following an ideology; split.

direct-action.rationale: Movement works through electoral politics; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative politics is not a theme of neo-nationalism; neutral inference.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivism is absent from neo-nationalism, which cherishes national economic strength; inferred disagreement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist utopian aim wholly outside the movement's concerns; inferred disagreement.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not held; work-based entitlement preferred in Orban's speech.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for need rather than profit is a socialist doctrine; the movement works with market economies, inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Neo-nationalists blame foreign competition and elites, not owners' profit as exploitation; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine alien to the ideology; inferred strong disagreement.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is not part of neo-nationalism; inferred strong disagreement.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Marxist theory of imperialism is not the movement's analysis, which blames globalisation and elites; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Some Western strands say so but nationalism relies on state; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Cultural-protection agenda justifies restrictions beyond harm; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nation as collective with rights is central; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Praise of armed forces but no documented stance on conscription; split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement values voting power and sovereign citizenship, not exit as the chief check; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts the idea of the nation as a community; inferred mild disagreement.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material-means freedom is not documented as a neo-nationalist theme; adherents are split.

media-academia-power.rationale: The address accuses an establishment of protecting itself, and the movement frames media and academic elites as hostile; moderate.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Wikipedia says neo-nationalism defines nation by historical association, not race; mainstream avoids race science.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist family and trade-body representation is not a plank of this movement; neutral inference.

total-state.rationale: Orbán and Trump alike speak of an accountable state serving citizens, not one directing all of life; inferred disagreement.

national-rebirth.rationale: Examples such as China's national rejuvenation and Trump's renewal rhetoric express rebirth, though not uniform.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mixed; Russia and Turkey expansionist, Western variants not.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oath-based authority has no place in a modern populist movement that appeals to the people; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is entirely foreign to the ideology; inferred strong disagreement.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed, though anti-academic rhetoric overlaps.

universal-morality.rationale: Particularist attachment is emphasised yet some invoke Christianity; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Populists speak of the people's single interest against elites; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Israel's Likud is listed as a neo-nationalist party, but other adherents are indifferent; split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Some governments grant diaspora citizenship and others do not, so adherents differ by country.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival matters for some national movements but is not documented for neo-nationalism; neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Co-determination is not part of the movement's agenda; mild disagreement inferred from business-friendly strands.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not addressed in sources and adherents vary by country.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal doctrine is not documented for neo-nationalism, and governments of the movement have both run deficits and balanced budgets.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mixed; critique of neoliberalism against free-market views.

rule-by-example.rationale: The address speaks of leading by example in foreign affairs only.

national-self-determination.rationale: Transfers of sovereignty are objected to because they weaken national self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Sovereignty first and scepticism of international bodies implies willingness; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Some neo-nationalists stress Christian tradition while others are secular; the movement is split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Opposition to immigration and nation-first logic imply welfare for citizens; Orban and others follow it, though sources treat welfare only indirectly.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Orban's work-based society ties benefits to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: The address calls for national unity across divides.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Protecting symbolic heritage such as art and folk traditions is a documented feature, so sacrificing institutions for novelty is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: A front of dominated countries is not a typical neo-nationalist idea, though Russia and China-style variants sometimes echo it.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement appeals to working and middle-class voters on national rather than international lines, which this statement describes; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditionalist strands favour distinct roles while others, such as some western leaders, do not; adherents are split.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest bans are not a neo-nationalist idea outside certain Islamic variants; inferred disagreement.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement distinguishes itself from racial nationalism via historical association.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Neo-nationalism sees the state as the nation's instrument, not a ruling-class tool; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Nationalist energy self-sufficiency and anti-climate-regime leanings; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Membership by historical association of the nation implies integration into the national culture; moderate.

elite-replacement.rationale: Present among some fringes but not mainstream; split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral-system preferences vary by country and are undocumented, so neutral.

national-mission.rationale: The address disclaims imposing its way of life on others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Adherents typically reject structural-patriarchy claims as part of cultural politics; inferred, not documented.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Trump's address says a small group in the capital reaped the rewards while citizens bore the cost, and anti-elite populism is central to the movement.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic sterilisation is not a position of mainstream neo-nationalism, which distinguishes itself from racial doctrines; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The address praises troops and police; legal accountability for past abuses is not favoured; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Neo-nationalists want state action on borders, jobs and trade, beyond a minimal state; inferred disagreement.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Membership is by historical association instead of race, according to the main reference, so racial discouragement is not a core stance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Trump said no room for prejudice in patriotism, but citizens favoured over foreigners; inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that the ideology does not engage; neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents reject framing their own states as colonial projects; inferred rather than documented.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One national law for all fits unified national identity; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is absent from the sources and varies sharply by country such as India or Turkey.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Specific to Indian politics; Hindu-nationalist BJP is listed but other adherents have no stance, so split.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in schools varies by country, with Poland and Hungary different from the UK; adherents split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine not relevant to this ideology; neutral.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The address says government returns power to the people; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionist economic nationalism favours exporting; moderate.

population-transfer.rationale: Mainstream neo-nationalists oppose immigration but do not generally call for expelling citizen minorities; mild disagreement inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Absolute non-aggression is a libertarian principle that neo-nationalists, who endorse strong police and military, do not hold; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Orban stresses national competitiveness but not progress as thesis; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents often claim to be targeted by such bans; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept of freedom is not discussed by neo-nationalist sources; neutral.

separated-powers.rationale: Orban's illiberal approach is criticized for weakening independent institutions, while Western strands keep checks; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist idea outside the movement; inferred strong disagreement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The movement speaks for the left-behind of the nation, but priority to the poor as a principle is not documented; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy varies by country and is undocumented here; neutral.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Right-leaning parties have restricted strikes while populist ones court workers; adherents split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty explanations in sources centre on globalisation and elites, not population; mild disagreement inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Opposition to multiculturalism rests on threat to national identity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition has no place in a movement built around elected populist leaders; inferred disagreement.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Orbán and others used emergency powers, but Western adherents defend civil liberties; contested.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls have been used in Hungary but are not a general plank; split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Western strands object; authoritarian ones differ.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is a communist practice; inferred disagreement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Opposition to immigration implies a restrictive route to citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric exists but a pay cap for representatives is not documented; neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline varies among populist parties and is undocumented here.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Hostile to the EU as a transnational quasi-state.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential versus parliamentary systems vary by country and the sources are silent.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the movement's concerns; neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy contradicts nationalist politics even in religion-friendly variants; inferred disagreement.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Neo-nationalism treats patriotism as binding, so working for one's own government's defeat is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Some adherents back moral censorship while others defend free expression; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits vary by country and some leaders have extended tenure while others oppose it; split.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a populist device but is not documented for this movement; neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The address commits to reinforce old alliances yet puts burden-sharing questions; adherents split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A radical housing doctrine foreign to the movement; inferred disagreement.

people-in-arms.rationale: Neo-nationalists favour professional armed forces and law enforcement, per the address; mild disagreement inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Some adherents romanticise the countryside but the movement draws from towns too; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Applies to Korea, Ireland and other cases; adherents differ by country and the sources are silent.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-establishment populism often casts educated elites as out of touch; moderate.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Defence of one's own heritage as worth protecting implies ranking attachments; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Positions differ across countries, such as the US versus Western Europe; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Traditionalist strands oppose sex-education and gender equality curricula; inferred, not documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: US evangelical-aligned adherents may favour this while others do not; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Cultural-traditionalists want limits while secular strands do not; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Membership is by historical association rather than ethnicity, so neither birth nor descent is pure.

minority-language-support.rationale: The stress on one national culture suggests reluctance to fund minority languages; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Tradition-defending outlook disfavours promoting nonconformity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The movement's nation-first stance and distrust of foreign aid imply no support for cancelling debts; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economic arguments are not part of the documented neo-nationalist programme; neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution drafting differs by country and the sources are silent.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Orban cites non-liberal states as models, but Western adherents disagree; split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nation first and the address criticizes spending abroad while home decays.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Sovereignty emphasis suggests independent deterrence is valued, but this is inferred not stated.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential systems and parliaments both exist among adherents; split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Populist scepticism of unaccountable institutions; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Israel's Likud and others say yes while others have no equivalent claim; split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property-as-social-function is not a documented neo-nationalist idea; neutral.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate in left-wing theory that the movement does not address; neutral.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from resistance to regulatory regimes.

collective-defense.rationale: The address commits to reinforce alliances; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Positions depend on the country and cause; Russia and others differ from Western variants.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Some adherents defend churches as national heritage; the movement is not anti-clerical; mild disagreement inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Neo-nationalist leaders are mostly partisan figures; but countries with ceremonial heads vary, so split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity stress suggests support for keeping the state whole; inferred, not documented.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country two systems is specific to China and Hong Kong; adherents have no common position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine rulers are alien to the populist movement, though Japanese nationalism is mentioned; inferred disagreement.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax design varies among right-leaning governments, such as Hungary versus others; split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Debate on nature and nurture is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Neo-nationalists claim democratic mandates and constitutional rules; ruler above law is not endorsed; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is not a documented goal of the movement; neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed regime theory is not engaged by the movement; neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Personality cults appear in Russia and elsewhere but Western adherents do not seek them; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law differs by country; Hungary and others have debated it, but the sources are silent.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist thesis outside the ideology; inferred disagreement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Estate seizures are a leftist doctrine at odds with the movement's property-respecting right; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement opposes accepting refugees, and favouring their return is a different issue; mild disagreement inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims for kin abroad appear in Hungary and Russia but not among most Western variants; split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing religious exit is alien to nearly all adherents; inferred strong disagreement.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering is not part of neo-nationalism, which in the West opposes Islamic dress; inferred disagreement.

common-currency.rationale: Hostile to EU integration and sovereignty transfers.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unions run against the nation-state focus, though some Eurasianist variants support them; mild disagreement.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Orban's declared illiberal state and the movement's critique of liberal democracy as the ideology of a transnational order rest on this.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the strand defends one national culture and identity as the basis of the state, so separate self-governing minority institutions cut against it.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: nationalists generally hold that nations are secure in their own homelands, though this strand has no documented position on persecuted minorities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses identity, culture and sovereignty over economic determinism, though it also cites economic grievances.

ban-cartels.rationale: Adherents are split: anti-elite populists attack concentrated corporate power while governments such as Orban's favour national champions; no shared line is documented.

no-bailouts.rationale: Adherents are split between populist hostility to elite bailouts and support for protecting national industry; no common position is documented.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the strand's emphasis on traditional family and national tradition and its distrust of imposed quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The overview lists protectionism and nation-first economics, and Trump's address says protection leads to prosperity; full closure to trade is not demanded, so only mild agreement.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: the strand opposes binding supranational rules on national policy, though some leaders favour trade terms that protect domestic workers.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred: the strand praises work and duty to the nation, as in Orban's work-based society, but does not seek to replace pay with moral incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred: the strand works through elections and existing institutions and does not advocate armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: the strand defends inherited national tradition and does not campaign against titles, though it has no stated position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Neo-nationalism defends national identity, culture and history against globalisation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sovereignty and national self-determination are central, so tutelage over others is inferred as rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Trump's inaugural address calls for total allegiance to the United States and national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Nation-first, colour-blind civic framing leads most adherents to oppose preferences; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: No common line on monetary reform; inferred as neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Market-friendly nationalists mostly accept capitalism as adaptable; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Adherents are split, from Orban's outreach to kin abroad to America First restraint.

delink-world-market.rationale: Neo-nationalists favour protectionism and sovereignty, not breaking with rich countries; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not a core view; nation-first welfare chauvinism rejects the framing; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not a defining position; most adherents accept some anti-discrimination law; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Adherents are split between constitutionalist and illiberal-majoritarian strands (Trump versus Orban).

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: a sovereignty-focused movement distrusts borders imposed from outside, though it is not a stated theme.

elective-rulers.rationale: Neo-nationalists back elective leaders in practice but the sources do not state a view on monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement favours majority will over minority checks.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: No documented position; adherents also praise strong leaders.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: national sovereignty is vested in national institutions against supranational bodies.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: humane use is the mainstream default.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No documented position; welfare chauvinism appears but not a duty of the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: a mobilising populist movement is politically engaged.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: adherents cast media and cultural elites as hostile, not as pacifying the public.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No documented position on consent versus force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: anti-globalisation rhetoric blames the world economy for domestic loss.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: a nation-first policy, as in the Inaugural Address, leans toward citizens in public roles.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties, outside the movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The America First address favours own-resource rebuilding over foreign dependence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: Orban-style politics has made revising the Trianon losses a recurring theme.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement defends the existing national majority.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement is hostile to what it sees as left-wing cultural frames.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: right-populists commonly condemn both fascism and communism as totalitarian.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement defends national heritage against cultural revision.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: right-populists often take up male-disadvantage claims.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: right-populists often take up this claim.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The illiberal-state speech says Western liberal models are not the only legitimate form for a nation.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement works through elected politics, not military guardianship.

filial-duty.rationale: Nation-first and traditional-values currents stress family and generational duty, but the movement has no documented line on it; inferred from that cultural conservatism.

office-by-exam.rationale: Neo-nationalists claim to speak for ordinary voters against unelected elites, so rule by examined officials sits badly with them; inferred from the anti-elite populism.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protectionism and economic nationalism lead adherents to back screening or blocking foreign purchases of key national firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Adherents are split between socially conservative and secular-liberal strands, and no shared position is documented.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The movement favors popular sovereignty and referendums but works through strong elected leaders rather than instructed, recallable delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Welfare-chauvinist parties often defend state pensions for citizens, though market-leaning ones differ; inferred as a lean against privatisation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Neo-nationalism defends private property within a national framework and has no tradition of communal land tenure; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Neo-nationalists in the mainstream operate within elected legislatures and do not campaign against parliamentary budget control, though they distrust supranational bodies; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: National-identity politics favors a common national language for public life and schooling, as in the focus on shared culture and assimilation.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nation-first sovereignty and border politics point toward restricting foreign land purchases, as in Orban-era Hungarian limits, but it is not a defining plank; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement rejects identity-based group remedies and holds that discrimination means unequal treatment rather than unequal outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Adherents are split: some criticise globalised consumer culture while others embrace market enjoyment; no common position is documented.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: America First and sovereigntist rhetoric opposes foreign entanglements and interference abroad, so adherents lean against arming rebels; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The movement champions every nation deciding its own affairs and opposes bloc discipline over members, as in its stance on the EU.

corporate-influence.rationale: Trump's address says a small group in the capital reaped rewards while citizens did not share them, which echoes complaints of elite and business capture.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the illiberal-state sovereignty stance and Hungary's laws on foreign-funded NGOs; the source speech does not state it directly.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Orban's family-centred nation-building; the cited speech does not set out the policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from nativism and protection of the national community's assets; no explicit policy in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Trump's address promises jobs and to Buy American and Hire American, but a state job guarantee is not stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: The inaugural address says nations should put their own interests first and that the US does not seek to impose its way of life, so it does not see spreading democracy as a route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: the strand values order and national institutions, so a general disclaimer of any duty to obey is unlikely.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the address's rejection of imposing one's way of life; an absolute ban for any reason is stronger than most adherents state.

industrial-unions.rationale: No union programme is attached to the strand; adherents are split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The strand excludes the explicitly racial far right, and mainstream adherents disavow minority-conspiracy claims, though elite-plot language appears.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Christian-national, family-centred illiberal programme.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: populists attack elite secrecy but illiberal governments restrict access, so adherents are split.

local-production.rationale: The address's call to Buy American and protect borders from foreign producers points to preferring national production, though not to local production as such.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the strand works through parties and movements and stresses state power, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Neo-nationalism defends national sovereignty against supranational bodies such as the EU, which implies national law outranks international courts.

religious-nation.rationale: Orban's speech casts Christian-national values as the basis of the state, but the strand mostly defines the nation by history and culture; adherents differ.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: its nation-first stance rejects subordination to other powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: No shared position; it varies by country.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the movement challenges personal property and it opposes socialism.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: neo-nationalists generally define themselves against socialism and communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Adherents are split between market-leaning and welfare-chauvinist positions.

religion-illusion.rationale: The overview records a defence of national religious and cultural heritage, and Orban defends a Christian-based national order.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: leaders such as Trump and Orban back market economies and national industry.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the movement is socially conservative on family and gender, though strands differ.

socialized-care.rationale: Orban's work-based society and family emphasis point to private family care; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: No shared position; language defence varies by country.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses sovereignty with no common stance on such treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: its individualist and national-state focus does not favour communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: No shared position; mainstream strands stress borders more than settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Some claim to reject both globalism and socialism, but no common doctrine; split.

missingStatements.text: Membership of a nation should rest on shared history and culture rather than on ethnic descent.
missingStatements.rationale: The overview describes historical association rather than ethnic or racial criteria as the defining trait separating neo-nationalism from classical nationalism.

missingStatements.text: A liberal democracy's courts and institutions should not constrain what a national majority has chosen.
missingStatements.rationale: Orban's declared illiberal state and the movement's critique of liberal democracy as the ideology of a transnational order rest on this.

notes: Highly heterogeneous across countries: economic, religious and gender positions differ between Trump-style, Orban-style and Meloni-style adherents, so many answers are low confidence and neutral.
